solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rank figure, American

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a figure
US, short for United States, as an adjective American

explanation.surface: A list of ranked statistics for an American, as if in a sports table.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is a person's standing or position in a hierarchy, a synonym of rank.

clue.text: Time left in America — in Oklahoma City

indicators.note: in says left is put inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: USA, the United States of America

explanation.surface: A timetable leaving from somewhere in America's Oklahoma City.
explanation.walkthrough: Oklahoma City is the state capital, but here the definition just means a city in Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is the second-largest urban centre in the state of Oklahoma.

clue.text: Felt hat must be arranged for horse racing

indicators.note: must be arranged says the letters of the words before are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A felt hat has to be sorted out for a day at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flat is British flat racing, run without jumps, as opposed to steeplechasing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flat is the name for the horse-racing season and code run over courses with no fences.

clue.text: Some oasis siesta for weaklings!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking a nap at a desert watering hole is only for the feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sissies are timid or feeble people, a mocking word for weaklings.

clue.text: Bizarrely, lets us fight

indicators.note: something done bizarrely is done in a strange, jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd invitation: someone strangely allows us to start a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous struggle or scuffle, a synonym of a fight.

clue.text: Edward possesses leg with firm muscles perhaps

indicators.note: possesses says Edward holds the leg inside him

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A man called Edward has a muscular leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned describes a body made firm and defined by exercise; muscles are one example.

clue.text: Name for Russian band: ace!

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the body
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A shout praising a Russian musical group as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group, but here it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasha is a common Russian diminutive of Alexander or Alexandra, a first name.

clue.text: An earl I troubled for old script

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A worried aristocrat confesses to studying an ancient writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear A is an undeciphered writing system of Minoan Crete, a very ancient script.

clue.text: Misses alarm, perhaps, as crackpot pens lies

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the letters of the words that follow are put in a crazy order

explanation.surface: A deluded person oversleeps while their pen writes falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as one example: missing the alarm is one way to stay in bed late.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep in is to stay in bed past the usual waking time, which typically follows ignoring an alarm clock.

clue.text: Wickedness by day in old Indian province

parts.note: sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: Moral decay in a historic region of the Indian subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sind, now usually spelt Sindh, was a province of British India and is now in Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sind was an administrative region under British rule in India, so it counts as an old province there.

clue.text: Lack of success oddly feasible

indicators.note: oddly says take the odd-numbered letters, the first, third, fifth and seventh, of the next word

explanation.surface: A plan that is strangely workable still turns out unsuccessful.
explanation.definitionFit: A fail is a failure, an outcome lacking any success, as in a school grade.

clue.text: American at home with English princess by noon

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: Someone is home with a British royal at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indianan is a native of Indiana, a US state, so is one kind of American.

clue.text: In charge of energy reserve

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone in control of the power supply held back in store.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun, ice means cool reserve in manner, as in 'break the ice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice can mean emotional coldness or aloofness, which is the reserve of a distant person.

clue.text: Stake placed between poles in French port

indicators.note: placed between says the stake goes in the middle of the two poles

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
an ante is a gambling stake put up before play

explanation.surface: A wooden stake is driven between two posts in a harbour town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city on the Loire with a historic river port in western France.

clue.text: In place of learning, rotter's in A&E with me!

indicators.note: in says the rotter is placed inside A&E

parts.note: A and E, the letters of the hospital department name without the ampersand
a cad is a rotter; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a scoundrel is in the casualty ward with them, when they should be at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department, Accident and Emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of universities and scholarship, a place devoted to study.

clue.text: A long time: no point reflecting

indicators.note: reflecting, like a mirror image, says the letters are turned backwards

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Spending ages thinking turns out to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long period, an age.

clue.text: SI units recalled in some universal settings

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Standard scientific measures brought to mind in general laboratory conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: The tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density, named after Nikola Tesla.

clue.text: Someone with book perhaps following close to street walker

indicators.note: following says the reader comes after the letter from street
close here means the end, so it picks the final letter of street

parts.note: a reader is someone with a book

explanation.surface: A person carrying a book walks along behind someone near the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A treader is one who treads, someone going on foot, a pedestrian.

clue.text: Small auto, crimson, permanently marked

parts.note: an auto is a car
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A little red car with lasting damage to its bodywork.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarred means left with a scar, a lasting mark from a wound or damage.

clue.text: Smith, for example, to endure celebrity

parts.note: to last is to endure
a name is a famous person, as in 'a big name'

explanation.surface: A blacksmith hoping to survive and become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Smith looks like a worker at a forge, but it is the commonest English surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Smith is an example of a surname, the family name that comes after a given name.

clue.text: Maybe Henry VIII's part you tried to discover last of all

indicators.note: last of all says take the final letter of every one of the words that come before

explanation.surface: A role a performer tried out to discover something about the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' shows Henry VIII is one example of the royal house the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII belonged to the Tudor dynasty, so anything of his is Tudor in style or period.

clue.text: Leading article by teacher

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a head is a head teacher

explanation.surface: A main piece of writing produced by a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means in front, which is where a leader is placed in a race.

clue.text: A film's ending in French: Let It Be?

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word film

parts.note: en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A movie's closing scene in French set to a Beatles song title.
explanation.walkthrough: Let It Be suggests the Beatles song, but read as a phrase it is what the word said at the end of a prayer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen, said after a prayer, means 'so be it', which is close to 'let it be'.

clue.text: Each day before run, start to yawn

parts.note: an eve is the day before an event
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the word yawn

explanation.surface: Every day ahead of a jog, someone begins yawning.
explanation.definitionFit: Every and each both mean all individual members of a group taken one by one.

clue.text: Fix guys drinks at the start

parts.note: guys are men

indicators.note: at the start picks the opening letter of the word drinks

explanation.surface: Someone arranges drinks for the lads first thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to repair it, a synonym of fix.

clue.text: Person assigned ne'er does badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put into a poor, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A ne'er-do-well, someone given a job, performs poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsee is the person to whom a cheque or bill is signed over, that is, assigned.

clue.text: Notice socialist fume

parts.note: to see is to notice
red is a common label for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Spotting a left-winger makes someone angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming furious, which is what fuming means.

clue.text: Overnight flight the fault of photographer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a late-night flight arriving early in the morning
second meaning: the red pupils a camera flash can cause in photos

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the second sense: the effect is in the picture, blamed on whoever took it.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both a tiring night-time plane journey and the red glare of flash photography on pupils.
